title: Check Whether a Word Is a Palindrome
statement: Given a word, return true if it reads the same forward and backward.
think: What is the task asking? Compare mirrored characters from the front and the back.
What is the key operation? Check whether pairs from both ends are equal.
What wording signals stand out? Palindrome, reads the same backward.
What is the brute force idea? Reverse the string and compare with the original.
What is the better/optimal idea? Compare characters in place with two pointers.
What are the edge cases? One character, even length, odd length.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(1) extra space if using direct comparison.
How would I explain it in an interview? I compare the outer characters first and move inward.
interview: I would use two pointers, one from each end, and compare mirrored characters while moving inward.
ru: Палиндром почти всегда сигнал на two pointers: сравниваем левый и правый край и идём к центру.
visualExplanation:
word = "level"
l e v e l
^       ^ -> same
  ^   ^ -> same
center reached -> true

critical: Compare only first and last characters

gaps: Nice to have: speak confidently about left/right pointers
constraints: Assume input is already a clean word.
whyThisPattern: This is a Two Pointers problem because palindrome checking compares mirrored positions from both ends.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not HashSet, because uniqueness is unrelated.
Not Sliding Window, because there is no moving substring window.
